requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.cli.overview_skill` has two obligations. Habeas must bundle a `habeas` skill. That skill's description must tell agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project. The description must also name four signs of such a project: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code.

The test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_used_at_the_start_of_any_work_in_a_habeas_project]` covers both.
- It reads the description through the helper `description("habeas")`. That helper reads the `description:` front-matter line of the `SKILL.md` embedded with `include_str!` in `skill_files`, so the check runs against the bundled asset.
- It asserts the description starts with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". That covers the "use at the start of any work" instruction.
- It loops over the four signs and asserts the description contains each one. The failure message names the missing sign. The four signs correspond one-to-one to the four named in the requirement.

I read the actual description in `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`. It contains the opening phrase and all four signs, so the assertions match the requirement and can fail if any sign or the opening phrase is removed.

I found no untested clause. Whether the skill is installed or exposed through the CLI is outside this requirement's text, which only says the skill is bundled and what its description says. The test is marked `{test}` for the requirement.
